verdict.text: Both findings sent back are fixed.
Every OpenViking request now takes a slot from one shared channel inside `send`, so workers and catch-up together stay at or under POOL_SIZE.
A slot is never held while waiting on the tree lock, so the folder-delete lock cannot deadlock against the slots.
Catch-up now lists one folder per request, pages with node_limit, offset and has_more, and walks the tree level by level.
Its paging matches the real OpenViking route.
Two small nits remain (gofmt in main.go and one unwrapped doc line).
f3 is still open as deferred hardening.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: green, stamp 2e0d600131be44e094e77f80e7dc4a12e97ef6fa9d480af228f202c14ce929f6, with pre_commit, cli_tests and rows r1 to r11 all passing.
Deadlock: `send` gets the slot after any lock the caller holds and frees it once the body is read.
Apply takes RLock and then a slot.
remove takes RLock and a slot for the file delete, lets both go, then takes Lock and slots one request at a time.
A goroutine waiting on the lock never holds a slot, so a slot holder is always in an HTTP request that ends (150 s client timeout).
Neither path takes the RWMutex twice.
Catch-up calls Apply and remove only after Walk returns, so it holds no lock while it walks.
Slot setup: `sync.Once` builds the channel on first use.
MaxInFlight is set to `pool` in main.go.
The send waits on ctx, so shutdown is not stuck on a full channel.
Real route: read `server/routers/filesystem.py` `ls`, `service/fs_service.py` `ls`, and `storage/viking_fs/_ops.py` `_ls_browsable_items`.
The server fetches node_limit+1 and sets has_more when there is more.
Offset skips entries after the hidden filter, which show_all_hidden turns off, so the client's `offset=len(entries)` is right.
The envelope's `has_more` sits next to `result` (`ListingResponse`), which matches `envelope.HasMore`.
The fake's ls does the same: sorted, offset, limit, has_more, 404 for a missing folder, and recursive capped at three levels.
r8 / TestConsumerPoolBound: CatchUp now runs in a loop during the 200-event burst.
It has 40 stale files, so its listings, deletes and folder removals race the workers.
The test fails if the peak measured inside the fake goes over Pool, and it waits for the deletes to finish, so the catch-up traffic really overlaps the burst.
Without the shared slots the peak would go over 4.
TestCatchUpListsWholeTree: 1200 files in one folder (above the 1000 page size) and one file five levels deep.
It fails on any write or delete.
A client that dropped has_more or relied on recursive ls would rewrite files and fail the test.
Docs: the components page (lines 93 to 97, 121 to 125, invariant table), the jobspec comment, and the Consumer.Pool and OpenViking.MaxInFlight docstrings now say what the code does.
